subject: sr-business-studies
title: Business Environment
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: A firm decides to train its staff to use the latest android software. This is a response to which environmental change?
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Which factor is included in the economic environment?
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of the legal environment?
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Which of the following is a part of the legal environment?
questions.answer: B

questions.q: The process of eliminating unnecessary controls and restrictions on the smooth functioning of business is called —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Creating digital infrastructure, delivering government services digitally and digital literacy are components of —
questions.answer: C

questions.q: To provide goods of standard quality is the responsibility of business towards —
questions.answer: C

questions.q: The element of business environment shaped by beliefs and customs of people is —
questions.answer: C

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of business environment?
questions.answer: D

questions.q: Creating a website and selling online is related to which environment?
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Infosys opening schools for less privileged children is an example of ______ environment.
questions.answer: D

questions.q: Fiscal policy deals with —
options: public expenditure, taxation and public debt
questions.answer: A

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Identify the type of business environment: (a) Includes the set of laws and regulations which influence business organisations. (b) Includes methods, techniques and approaches for production of goods and services.
questions.answer: (a) Legal environment. (b) Technological environment.

questions.q: Identify the interest group of business: (a) To pay taxes honestly and on time. (b) To provide reasonable and fair wages and salary.
questions.answer: (a) Government. (b) Employees.

questions.q: Name any two factors included under demographic environment.
questions.answer: Size, density, distribution and growth rate of population (also age composition).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks regarding the 1991 reforms: (a) ______ refers to eliminating unnecessary controls and restrictions. (b) ______ refers to reducing the role of the public sector.
questions.answer: (a) Liberalisation. (b) Privatisation.

questions.q: State whether true or false: (a) The business environment is static in nature. (b) The changes in business environment are unpredictable.
questions.answer: (a) False. (b) True.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) The interaction between the business and its environment helps in identifying opportunities and threats. (ii) Environmental understanding does not help business organisations in improving their image.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) To ensure safety of investment is the responsibility of business towards its ______. (ii) To develop a sense of belonging is the responsibility towards its ______.
questions.answer: (i) shareholders (owners). (ii) employees.

questions.q: Identify the type of non-economic environment: (a) Demand for new clothes increases during festivals. (b) The computer has outdated the typewriter.
questions.answer: (a) Social environment. (b) Technological environment.

questions.q: Give the full form: (a) GST (b) FEMA.
questions.answer: (a) Goods and Services Tax. (b) Foreign Exchange Management Act.

questions.q: Name any two economic policies of the government.
questions.answer: Industrial policy, fiscal policy, monetary policy, foreign investment policy, Exim policy (any two).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: State any two objectives of the 'Make in India' initiative of the Government of India.
questions.answer: Expansion of job opportunities and ease of doing business; upgradation of technology and improving India's global ranking.

questions.q: State any two benefits of 'Digital India'.
questions.answer: It introduces e-services such as e-health and DigiLocker and gives easy access to information with less documentation.

questions.q: List any four economic policies.
questions.answer: Industrial policy, fiscal policy, monetary policy, foreign investment policy and export-import policy.

questions.q: How do judicial decisions constitute part of the legal environment?
questions.answer: Decisions of courts interpret laws and set precedents which businesses must follow, so they affect business conduct.

questions.q: State any two responsibilities of business towards the shareholders or owners.
questions.answer: To ensure safety of investment and to provide a fair and regular dividend (also information and capital appreciation).

questions.q: State any two features of business environment.
questions.answer: It is dynamic and uncertain; it is complex and inter-related.

questions.q: What is meant by globalisation?
questions.answer: Integrating the economy of a country with the world economy through free flow of goods, services, capital, technology and labour across borders.

questions.q: Mention any two causes of environmental pollution.
questions.answer: Carbon monoxide from automobiles and chemical waste from factories, plastic and excess pesticides.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the importance of business environment (any three points).
questions.answer: It helps determine opportunities and threats, gives direction for growth, supports continuous learning, builds image and helps meet competition.

questions.q: Explain the impact of government policy changes of 1991 on business.
questions.answer: Companies adopted world-class technology, customers became more demanding, competition from MNCs increased, businesses had to change policies and had to develop human resources.

questions.q: Explain the benefits of GST.
questions.answer: It eliminates tax on tax, is technology driven and online, lowers the cost of goods, speeds up taxation, reduces compliances and regularises the unorganised sector.

questions.q: Explain the responsibilities of business towards consumers.
questions.answer: Regular supply, reasonable prices, standard quality, true advertisements and prompt service and attention to complaints.

questions.q: Distinguish between social responsibility and legal obligation, and give three reasons for social responsibility.
questions.answer: Legal obligation is followed for fear of law; social responsibility is voluntary. Reasons: self-interest, public image and moral justification.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the dimensions of business environment (economic and non-economic) with examples.
questions.answer: Economic: conditions, policies and system (mixed economy). Non-economic: social (customs, literacy), political (stability), legal (Companies Act 2013), technological, demographic and natural environment, each influencing business decisions.

questions.q: Why is it significant for a business to understand its environment?
questions.answer: It identifies opportunities and threats, gives direction for growth, enables continuous learning, builds image, helps meet competition and shows strengths and weaknesses.

questions.q: Explain liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation and their impact on business.
questions.answer: Liberalisation removes controls; privatisation reduces the public sector's role; globalisation integrates the economy with the world; effects: technological change, demanding consumers, competition, need for change and human resource development.

questions.q: Explain the social responsibility of business towards different interest groups.
questions.answer: Towards owners (fair return), employees (fair wages), consumers (quality goods), government (taxes and laws) and the community (environment, employment, culture).
